title: Dual and opposing roles of the EXD2 exonuclease in the resolution of RNA-DNA hybrids.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the single Zenodo deposit (Figures.zip, 20,075,142 bytes, CC-BY-4.0) and unzipped it: 36 files totalling 24 MB in folders named 'Fig. 1'-'Fig. 5'. Contents are 16 OriginLab .opju project files (proprietary binary, unreadable without OriginPro; `file` reports only 'data'), 12 PNG screenshots of kymographs/images, and 8 spreadsheets. I parsed every spreadsheet with pandas: all sheets are headerless numeric blocks (e.g. 8,927 x 4 and 2,206 x 4 time traces; 11 x 11 and 9 x 8 summary tables), zero column names, zero units, and 12,133 '--' placeholder cells in one file alone. The largest per-condition sample is 11 values (Fig. 2c columns hold 11, 8 and 7 single-molecule measurements).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design (optical-tweezers single-molecule force spectroscopy on RNA-DNA hybrids, EXD2 condensation vs digestion, mitochondrial imaging), and the reported sample sizes n = 5, 7, 9 and 11 molecules per condition, which I grepped from the open-access full text. Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out after 135 s, so the journal supplement itself was not retrieved; Europe PMC reports no database cross-references (hasDbCrossReferences = N) and no GEO/SRA/BioProject links were found.

a1_downloadable.note: One Zenodo archive, open access, CC-BY-4.0, no login. I downloaded and extracted it (20 MB).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. There is no prediction target anywhere: every sheet is an unnamed numeric block of raw force/extension/fluorescence traces plotted in a figure. Any label (e.g. 'this molecule was digested' vs 'this molecule condensed') would have to be hand-constructed by annotating traces and reading figure legends.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL, verified. No sequences, no structures, no identifiers of any kind are in the deposit; the only 'input' is a raw instrument time trace, and 16 of 36 files (the majority of the numeric data) are locked in proprietary OriginLab .opju binaries.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL, verified. Not one column header or unit string exists in any of the 8 spreadsheets; units (pN, micrometres, seconds, nM) are implied only by the published figure axes.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified. The experimental unit is a single molecule, and the largest per-condition count in the files is 11 (Fig. 2c: 11, 8 and 7 values); the paper itself reports n = 5-11. The 8,927-row tables are time points inside one trace, not independent examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 24 MB unzipped; trivially fits. This is the only Part A item the dataset comfortably passes besides A1.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: the files carry no sample-size metadata, no per-molecule identifiers and no condition labels, so there is nothing to reconcile against the paper's n = 5-11.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists, so provenance cannot be traced. Any label a modeller invented would be their own reading of a trace, i.e. a hand annotation of the same signal used as the feature - leakage by construction.

controls.external_validation: No second dataset of EXD2 single-molecule traces was found; the related Nature Chemical Biology 2025 PARP1-EXD2 paper and the EMBO J 2022 EXD2 kinetics paper exist but their data were not checked and would be different assays.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available: with 5-11 single molecules per condition, unlabelled headerless traces and no units, any model fitted here would describe one instrument's output in one lab and could not be stated as a claim about EXD2 biology.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-molecule stretching traces to predict whether a protein will cut or instead protect an RNA-DNA hybrid.
plain_idea.train_on: What a modeller would see per example is one optical-tweezers time trace (force and molecule length over time, plus a fluorescence channel) for one RNA-DNA hybrid molecule. Verified count: at most 11 molecules per experimental condition, a few dozen traces in total.
plain_idea.predict: Which of the two outcomes the paper describes happened - the enzyme slowly digested the hybrid, or it clumped together with it and shielded it. The true answer comes from a human reading the same trace, not from an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If it worked, single-molecule labs could score traces automatically instead of by eye; as it stands the honest value of this deposit is as figure provenance, not as training data.

more_or_better_data.why: A few dozen traces from one instrument in one lab (verified: max 11 molecules per condition) is far smaller than anything the named R-loop predictors used, and it is a different data type (force traces, not genome sequence).

confidence_score.why: With 5-11 molecules per condition there is no way to estimate per-prediction uncertainty that anyone would trust; replicate structure exists only as 3 traces per panel.

models_beatable.why: The named models (deepRloopPre, DeepER) solve a different task - predicting R-loop sites along a genome from sequence and epigenomic tracks - so there is no comparison to win or lose here.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model takes this input, so it cannot be run as a baseline, and no new data measures the same quantity the same way; the first condition fails outright.

ml_idea: The only machine-learning task this deposit could support is automatic classification or segmentation of optical-tweezers traces (digestion vs condensation vs damage recognition). It dies on sample size and labels: a few dozen traces, no label column, no units, and 16 of 36 files in a proprietary OriginLab format. A better use of the paper is as biological motivation for a genomics project on R-loops - but that would need DRIP-seq style data from elsewhere, which this paper does not deposit.

effort.compute_note: Measured the archive (20 MB zipped, 24 MB unzipped) and parsed every spreadsheet in under a second on CPU; compute was never the constraint, data content was.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the independent molecules per condition in the figure source data - it is 11, 8 and 7 in Fig. 2c, which kills the project in five minutes.

verdict_reason: Verified in the files: the Zenodo deposit is per-figure plotting source data for a single-molecule biophysics study - 36 files, 16 of them proprietary OriginLab .opju binaries, 12 PNG screenshots, and 8 headerless spreadsheets with no column names and no units. There is no prediction target column (A2), no inputs beyond raw instrument traces (A3), no units (A4), and the experimental unit count is 5-11 molecules per condition against a ~1,500-row threshold (A5). Nothing in the deposit carries an identifier, so no integration or external validation is possible either.
